questions.question: Which Snowflake feature allows sharing compute costs with data consumers who don't have a Snowflake account?

options.text: Direct Share
Reader Account
Data Marketplace
External Tables

questions.explanation: B is correct. Reader Accounts (formerly Managed Accounts) allow data providers to create Snowflake accounts for consumers who don't have their own Snowflake account. The provider manages and pays for the reader account's compute costs. Direct Shares require consumers to have their own Snowflake account.

questions.question: What is the Snowflake Data Marketplace?

options.text: A platform for buying and selling Snowflake credits
A marketplace where data providers can publish datasets that consumers can access directly in their Snowflake accounts
An internal tool for managing database schemas
A tool for comparing pricing across cloud providers

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Snowflake Marketplace allows data providers to publish and monetize datasets. Data consumers can discover and access these datasets directly in their Snowflake accounts without any data copying or ETL required — data is accessed via Snowflake's secure data sharing.

questions.question: What is Snowflake Secure Data Sharing?

options.text: A feature that copies data from one account to another using ETL pipelines
A feature that allows sharing live, ready-to-query data between Snowflake accounts without copying or moving the data
A feature that exports data to external cloud storage for sharing
A feature that sends email notifications with data attachments to consumers

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake Secure Data Sharing enables sharing live data between accounts without any data copying, movement, or ETL. Consumers access the provider's data in place, ensuring they always see the most current version of the data.

questions.question: In Snowflake's data sharing model, who pays for the compute costs when a consumer queries shared data?

options.text: The data provider always pays
The data consumer pays using their own virtual warehouses
Costs are split equally between provider and consumer
Snowflake absorbs the compute costs

questions.explanation: B is correct. In Snowflake's data sharing model, the consumer pays for compute costs using their own virtual warehouses to query shared data. The provider owns and stores the data, but does not incur compute costs when consumers query it.

questions.question: Which SQL command is used to view the list of shares available in a Snowflake account?

options.text: LIST SHARES
DESCRIBE SHARES
SHOW SHARES
GET SHARES

questions.explanation: C is correct. The SHOW SHARES command lists all shares available in the account, including both outbound shares (created by the account) and inbound shares (shared to the account by other providers).

questions.question: What grant must be applied to a database created from a share so that users can access the shared objects?

options.text: GRANT USAGE ON DATABASE
GRANT IMPORTED PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES
GRANT OWNERSHIP ON DATABASE

questions.explanation: B is correct. When a database is created from a share, the IMPORTED PRIVILEGES grant must be used to allow other roles in the consumer account to access the shared objects. This single grant propagates all privileges defined by the provider's share.

questions.question: A share object in Snowflake can contain which of the following? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Tables
Secure views
Secure UDFs
Virtual warehouses

questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct. A share object can contain tables, secure views, and secure user-defined functions (UDFs). Virtual warehouses cannot be shared; each account manages its own compute resources independently.

questions.question: Which SQL command is used to add a consumer account to an existing share?

options.text: GRANT SHARE TO ACCOUNT
ADD ACCOUNT TO SHARE
ALTER SHARE SET ACCOUNTS =
UPDATE SHARE ADD ACCOUNT

questions.explanation: C is correct. The ALTER SHARE ... SET ACCOUNTS = command is used to add or update the list of consumer accounts that can access a share. You can also use ALTER SHARE ... ADD ACCOUNTS = to append accounts without replacing the existing list.

questions.question: What is the default requirement for Secure Data Sharing between two Snowflake accounts?

options.text: Both accounts must be in the same cloud provider and region
Both accounts must be on the same Snowflake edition
Both accounts must be owned by the same organization
Both accounts must use the same virtual warehouse size

questions.explanation: A is correct. By default, Secure Data Sharing requires both the provider and consumer accounts to be in the same cloud provider and region. Cross-region and cross-cloud sharing requires additional mechanisms such as listings with auto-fulfillment or database replication.

questions.question: What distinguishes a free listing from a paid listing on the Snowflake Marketplace?

options.text: Free listings are only available to Enterprise edition accounts
Free listings provide data at no charge, while paid listings require the consumer to pay the provider for data access
Paid listings allow data modification, while free listings are read-only
Free listings cannot contain secure views

questions.explanation: B is correct. Free listings on the Snowflake Marketplace allow consumers to access data at no charge from the provider, while paid listings require the consumer to pay the provider a fee for data access. In both cases, the consumer pays their own compute costs.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Snowflake Marketplace?

options.text: To sell Snowflake compute credits at discounted prices
To enable providers to publish and consumers to discover live, ready-to-query data products
To manage internal data governance policies
To replicate databases across cloud regions automatically

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Snowflake Marketplace is a platform where data providers can publish data products (datasets, ML models, applications) and consumers can discover, evaluate, and access them directly in their Snowflake accounts without data movement.

questions.question: Which types of data products can be published on the Snowflake Marketplace? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Standard datasets
Snowflake Native Apps
Virtual warehouse configurations
Data services backed by Snowpark functions

questions.explanation: A, B, and D are correct. The Snowflake Marketplace supports publishing standard datasets, Snowflake Native Apps, and data services. Virtual warehouse configurations are not a shareable data product type.

questions.question: What must a provider do before a listing becomes publicly available on the Snowflake Marketplace?

options.text: Pay a one-time publishing fee to Snowflake
Submit the listing for review and approval by Snowflake
Create a reader account for every potential consumer
Replicate the data to all available regions first

questions.explanation: B is correct. Before a listing becomes publicly visible on the Snowflake Marketplace, providers must submit it for review and approval by Snowflake. This ensures quality standards are met and the listing complies with Marketplace policies.

questions.question: How does a consumer access a Marketplace listing in their Snowflake account?

options.text: By downloading a data file and loading it into a table
By requesting access through the Marketplace and having a shared database created in their account
By cloning the provider's database using CREATE DATABASE ... CLONE
By connecting to the provider's account via an API endpoint

questions.explanation: B is correct. When a consumer gets a listing from the Marketplace, a shared database is created in their account, giving them direct access to the provider's data without any copying or ETL. The consumer can then query the data using their own compute resources.

questions.question: How can consumers discover listings on the Snowflake Marketplace?

options.text: Only through direct links shared by the provider
By browsing categories, searching by keyword, or filtering by provider and data type within the Marketplace
Only through Snowflake support tickets
By running SHOW MARKETPLACE LISTINGS in SQL

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Snowflake Marketplace provides search and discovery features including category browsing, keyword search, and filtering by provider, data type, and other attributes to help consumers find relevant data products.

questions.question: What is a public listing in the Snowflake Marketplace?

options.text: A listing visible only to accounts in the same organization
A listing visible to all Snowflake accounts that can browse the Marketplace
A listing that requires manual approval for each consumer
A listing that is only accessible via direct SQL commands

questions.explanation: B is correct. A public listing is visible to all Snowflake accounts that can browse the Marketplace. Any eligible consumer can discover and request access to a public listing without needing a direct invitation from the provider.

questions.question: What is a private listing in Snowflake?

options.text: A listing that encrypts all shared data with a consumer-managed key
A listing that is visible only to specifically invited consumer accounts
A listing that hides the provider's identity from consumers
A listing that restricts data access to a single database

questions.explanation: B is correct. A private listing is shared only with specific consumer accounts that the provider explicitly invites. Unlike public listings, private listings are not discoverable by browsing the Marketplace — only invited accounts can see and access them.

questions.question: What is a Snowflake Data Exchange?

options.text: A public marketplace open to all Snowflake users
A private, managed hub where a group of accounts can publish and share data among invited members
A tool for converting data between file formats
An ETL pipeline service built into Snowflake

questions.explanation: B is correct. A Data Exchange is a private, managed hub where a curated group of Snowflake accounts can publish and share data among its members. Unlike the public Marketplace, membership is controlled by the exchange administrator.

questions.question: A company wants to distribute shared datasets to multiple business partners across different organizations. Which Snowflake feature best supports this use case?

options.text: Database cloning
Listings (public or private) via the Snowflake Marketplace
External tables with shared storage
Snowpipe data loading

questions.explanation: B is correct. Listings via the Snowflake Marketplace (either public or private) provide the best mechanism for distributing data to multiple organizations. Listings support cross-organization sharing and can leverage auto-fulfillment for cross-region/cross-cloud delivery.

questions.question: What is the Snowflake Native App Framework?

options.text: A mobile SDK for building Snowflake client applications
A framework that allows providers to package data, code, and logic into an application that consumers install and run in their own Snowflake account
A framework for building external API integrations with Snowflake
A set of pre-built analytics dashboards provided by Snowflake

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Snowflake Native App Framework enables providers to build applications that bundle data, business logic, and UI components. Consumers install these apps directly in their own Snowflake accounts, running them with their own compute and against their own data.

questions.question: In the Snowflake Native App Framework, what is an application package?

options.text: A compressed ZIP file uploaded to a Snowflake stage
A Snowflake object that bundles the app's data, code, configuration, and version history for distribution
A Python library installed via pip
A Docker container image stored in a Snowflake registry

questions.explanation: B is correct. An application package is a Snowflake first-class object that contains the application's data content, code, configuration, and version history. Providers use application packages to define, version, and distribute their Native Apps to consumers.

questions.question: How does a consumer deploy a Snowflake Native App?

options.text: The consumer downloads the app source code and runs it locally
The consumer installs the app in their own Snowflake account, where it runs using their compute resources
The provider runs the app in their account on behalf of the consumer
The app runs in a shared Snowflake-managed environment outside both accounts

questions.explanation: B is correct. A Snowflake Native App is installed directly in the consumer's own Snowflake account. The consumer's compute resources are used to run the app, and the app can access the consumer's data with appropriate permissions granted during installation.

questions.question: What key advantage does the Native App Framework offer providers compared to traditional data sharing?

options.text: It allows sharing data without using shares
It enables providers to distribute code, business logic, and data together as a single installable product
It eliminates the need for consumer accounts
It automatically converts data into Parquet format

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Native App Framework goes beyond traditional data sharing by allowing providers to package and distribute code, business logic, stored procedures, and data together as a complete application product. This enables richer data products beyond raw data access.

questions.question: How can a provider monetize a Snowflake Native App?

options.text: By collecting payments outside of Snowflake only
By publishing the app as a paid listing on the Snowflake Marketplace
By charging consumers per query executed
By selling Snowflake credits earned from the app

questions.explanation: B is correct. Providers can monetize their Snowflake Native Apps by publishing them as paid listings on the Snowflake Marketplace. Snowflake handles billing and payment processing, allowing providers to set pricing for their applications.

questions.question: What is auto-fulfillment in the context of Snowflake data sharing?

options.text: Automatic backup of shared data to a secondary region
Automatic replication and delivery of listing data to consumers in different regions or cloud providers
Automatic approval of all consumer access requests
Automatic scaling of virtual warehouses during shared data queries

questions.explanation: B is correct. Auto-fulfillment automatically replicates and delivers listing data to consumers in different regions or cloud providers. This enables cross-region and cross-cloud sharing through listings without the provider manually setting up replication.

questions.question: What underlying technology does Snowflake use to enable cross-region data sharing?

options.text: External tables pointing to cross-region storage
Database replication to replicate data to the consumer's region
VPN tunneling between regions
Data export and import via cloud storage buckets

questions.explanation: B is correct. Cross-region data sharing in Snowflake leverages database replication behind the scenes. The data is replicated from the provider's region to the consumer's region, enabling consumers to query the data locally with low latency.

questions.question: How do listings enable cross-cloud sharing in Snowflake?

options.text: By converting data to a universal format readable by all cloud providers
By using auto-fulfillment to replicate data across cloud platforms (e.g., AWS to Azure)
By requiring both accounts to use the same cloud provider
By routing all queries through a central Snowflake-managed cloud

questions.explanation: B is correct. Listings with auto-fulfillment enable cross-cloud sharing by automatically replicating the provider's data to the consumer's cloud platform. This allows a provider on AWS to share data with a consumer on Azure or GCP seamlessly.

questions.question: What are the cost considerations for cross-region data sharing in Snowflake?

options.text: Cross-region sharing is always free
There are additional costs for data replication and cross-region data transfer
Only the consumer incurs additional costs for cross-region queries
Cross-region sharing costs the same as same-region sharing

questions.explanation: B is correct. Cross-region sharing incurs additional costs for data replication (compute and storage for maintaining a replica) and cross-region data transfer fees. These costs are above and beyond the standard compute costs for querying shared data.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about cross-region and cross-cloud sharing is true?

options.text: Direct shares can be used across regions without any additional setup
Listings with auto-fulfillment are the recommended approach for cross-region and cross-cloud sharing
Cross-cloud sharing is not supported in Snowflake
Cross-region sharing requires both accounts to upgrade to Business Critical edition

questions.explanation: B is correct. Listings with auto-fulfillment are the recommended approach for cross-region and cross-cloud sharing. Direct shares only work within the same region and cloud provider. Auto-fulfillment handles the data replication needed for cross-region/cross-cloud delivery.

questions.question: What are Snowflake Data Clean Rooms?

options.text: Isolated environments for cleaning and transforming raw data
Secure environments where multiple parties can collaborate on data analysis without exposing their raw data to each other
Staging areas for data quality checks before loading into production
Temporary databases used during data migration

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake Data Clean Rooms are secure environments that enable multiple parties to collaborate on data analysis without exposing their raw underlying data to each other. Only agreed-upon aggregated or anonymized results are shared between the parties.

questions.question: What is the key privacy-preserving principle of Snowflake Data Clean Rooms?

options.text: All data is encrypted with a shared key between parties
No party can see or access the other party's raw data; only approved queries and aggregated results are allowed
All data is anonymized before being loaded into the clean room
Data is deleted after each analysis session

questions.explanation: B is correct. The core privacy-preserving principle of Data Clean Rooms is that no party can directly see or access the other party's raw data. Only pre-approved queries can be run, and only aggregated or anonymized results are returned, ensuring data privacy is maintained.

questions.question: Which industries commonly use Snowflake Data Clean Rooms? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Advertising and media for audience overlap analysis
Healthcare for collaborative research without sharing patient data
Financial services for fraud detection across institutions
Manufacturing for machine calibration

questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct. Data Clean Rooms are widely used in advertising (audience overlap and campaign measurement), healthcare (collaborative research without exposing patient records), and financial services (cross-institution fraud analysis). These industries benefit most from privacy-preserving data collaboration.

questions.question: In a Data Clean Room scenario, what type of results can typically be accessed by the participating parties?

options.text: Full row-level data from all parties
Only aggregated or anonymized results from pre-approved queries
Raw data from the party that initiated the analysis
Encrypted copies of all participant data

questions.explanation: B is correct. In a Data Clean Room, participating parties can only access aggregated or anonymized results generated by pre-approved queries. Raw row-level data from any party is never exposed to other participants, preserving data privacy.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a Reader Account in Snowflake?

options.text: To allow users to read data documentation
To share data with consumers who do not have their own Snowflake account
To provide read-only access to internal users within the same account
To create backup copies of databases

questions.explanation: B is correct. Reader Accounts (formerly known as Managed Accounts) allow data providers to share data with external consumers who do not have their own Snowflake account. The provider creates and manages these accounts specifically for data sharing purposes.

questions.question: Who creates and manages Reader Accounts in Snowflake?

options.text: Snowflake automatically creates them for all consumers
The data consumer requests one through the Marketplace
The data provider creates and manages Reader Accounts
A Snowflake support engineer creates them upon request

questions.explanation: C is correct. The data provider is responsible for creating and managing Reader Accounts. The provider controls the account setup, user access, and resource allocation for each Reader Account they create.

questions.question: Who pays for the compute resources used in a Reader Account?

options.text: The consumer who uses the Reader Account
The data provider who created the Reader Account
Snowflake covers the compute costs
Compute costs are shared between provider and consumer

questions.explanation: B is correct. The data provider pays for all compute resources used in Reader Accounts they create. This is a key difference from regular data sharing where the consumer uses their own warehouses. Providers should monitor Reader Account usage to manage costs.

questions.question: Which of the following is a limitation of Reader Accounts compared to full Snowflake accounts?

options.text: Reader Accounts cannot run SQL queries
Reader Accounts cannot create their own databases or load data
Reader Accounts cannot use virtual warehouses
Reader Accounts cannot access shared data

questions.explanation: B is correct. Reader Accounts have significant limitations compared to full Snowflake accounts. They cannot create their own databases, load their own data, or perform other data management operations. They are limited to querying data that has been shared with them by the provider.

questions.question: A company wants to share data with a partner that uses a different cloud provider and does not have a Snowflake account. Which combination of features should they use?

options.text: Direct Share with database replication
Reader Account combined with a listing that uses auto-fulfillment
External tables with cross-cloud storage access
Snowpipe with a shared stage

questions.explanation: B is correct. Since the partner has no Snowflake account, a Reader Account is needed. Since they are on a different cloud provider, a listing with auto-fulfillment handles the cross-cloud replication. Together, these features solve both challenges.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about Reader Accounts? (Select all that apply)

options.text: They are created and managed by the data provider
The provider pays for the compute resources consumed
They can create their own databases and load external data
They allow non-Snowflake customers to query shared data

questions.explanation: A, B, and D are correct. Reader Accounts are created and managed by the data provider, who also pays for compute. They enable non-Snowflake customers to access shared data. Reader Accounts cannot create their own databases or load external data — they are limited to querying shared data only.

questions.question: What happens to shared data in a consumer's account if the provider revokes the share?

options.text: The consumer retains a cached copy of the data
The consumer immediately loses access to the shared data
The shared data is automatically cloned into the consumer's account
The consumer has a 30-day grace period before losing access

questions.explanation: B is correct. Since Secure Data Sharing does not copy data, the consumer accesses the provider's data in place. If the provider revokes the share (removes the consumer account from the share), the consumer immediately loses access. No data copy exists in the consumer's account.

questions.question: Which Snowflake edition is required at minimum to use Secure Data Sharing as a provider?

options.text: Standard
Enterprise
Business Critical
Virtual Private Snowflake (VPS)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Secure Data Sharing is available in all Snowflake editions, including Standard. Any Snowflake account can create shares and act as a data provider, regardless of the edition.
